ob-nūbo , psi, ptum, 3,
I.v. a., to veil, cover (very rare; syn.: velo, induo, amicio).
I. Lit.: LICTOR, CONLIGA MANVS, CAPVT OBNVBITO, ARBORI INFELICI SVSPENDITO, an old formula ap. Cic. Rab. Perd. 4, 13: flammeo caput nubentis obvolvatur, quod antiqui obnubere vocarint ... legem jubere caput ejus obnubere qui parentem necavisset, quod est obvolvere, Paul. ex Fest. p. 170 Müll.; Liv. 1, 26; Val. Fl. 2, 254: “ca put tempestate,” Sil. 11, 259 : comas amictu Verg. A. 11, 77.—Absol., to veil the head
obnubit, caput operit, Paul. ex Fest. p. 184 Müll.—*
II. Transf.: “mare terras obnubit,” Varr. L. L. 5, § 72 Müll.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
